method: Each of the four original captures and marketing image per ID inspected with vision_analyze before consulting relevant parent ledger entries. No contact sheets substituted.
scope_limitations: Static endpoints cannot certify mechanics, hinge contact, collision-free motion, hidden surfaces, or complete cavity floors.
Marketing is a promotional reference, not exact model geometry or approval evidence.
Prominent dark lid seams also occur in marketing; they alone do not establish closure failure. Raised open-state clasp tabs and concealed exterior lid ornaments are not by themselves defects.

geometry_observations: Closed desktop and mobile preserve raised eroded terrain, rectangular body, round front fitting, clasp, side ring and rock-like feet; no clear missing face or gross intersection.

Both open views show an intact-looking empty cavity and raised patterned lid. Near-left rim has a conspicuous notch/stepped junction; hinge attachment is partly obscured rather than demonstrably detached.
Dark closed seam is pronounced in viewer and reference; exposed inner strips and corner steps warrant caution but do not prove failed seating.
finish_limitations: Repeated ochre/orange waves read more regular than naturally weathered strata; terrain and feet are angular against the softer reference.
Brass is subdued and simplified; interior pattern reduces depth separation.
entries.framing: All four original views contain the full chest, feet and raised hardware without obvious clipping; mobile controls fit, though fine hardware and secondary text are small.
entries.reason: Broad reference identity and visible cavity remain coherent; no unequivocal structural defect. Rim and hinge contacts remain unresolved static-view limitations.

geometry_observations: Closed views show coherent copper-colored body, medallion, corner caps, front clasp and block feet; prominent dark seam also occurs in reference.
Open desktop/mobile show hollow cavity and two rear hinges; layered rim/corner joints are blocky, attachment obscured, with no proven missing face or detachment.
Botanical ornament is on the outward lid face; its absence from the visible inner lid in open views is not missing geometry.
finish_limitations: Viewer medallion reads as botanical relief, while marketing shows a more angular radial/petal ornament within concentric rings; exact equivalence is not demonstrated.
Copper reads orange and broadly mottled rather than distinct hammered depressions. Marketing is browner/woodlike with softer satin highlights; brass details are simplified.
entries.framing: All four original views frame the entire object and controls; no obvious mobile overflow. Fine joinery remains small.
entries.reason: Retain parent ornament-fidelity decision hold. No definite structural failure is established, but botanical versus radial ornament treatment needs an explicit acceptance decision.

geometry_observations: Both closed captures retain joined tower architecture, pale conical roofs, open-topped cylinder, front clasp/disc, corner fittings and short feet.
Open views show raised lid and empty cavity with defined inner walls, stepped rim corners and visible hinges. No obvious broken face or hole; rear joins and hinge contacts remain uncertain.
Dark closed seam also exists in marketing and is not independently proof of misclosure.
finish_limitations: Viewer earth texture is soft/mottled and roofs more angular/grainy; marketing has richer plaster grain and distinctly ribbed woven-looking roof detail.
Inner lid has subtle rectangular tonal patches; plain interior and relatively flat brass limit realism rather than establish damage.
entries.framing: Chest, architectural lid, feet and open-state tab fit both desktop and mobile; buttons fit side by side, with small secondary text.
entries.reason: Architectural identity and coherent visible open cavity preserved. No unequivocal geometry or framing failure; differences are primarily finish/detail fidelity.

geometry_observations: Closed views retain three capped courtyard forms, low surrounding rails, cream stripes/feet, dark front accents, clasp/disc and side ring.
Open views reveal intact-looking raised lid and cavity walls. Protruding rim ends and stepped corner joins are conspicuous but do not establish holes or broken geometry.
Wide dark seam appears in reference as well as viewer; hidden hinge attachments cannot be certified.
finish_limitations: Viewer is warmer terracotta/orange with angular trim and feet; marketing is softer salmon/pink with more rounded highlights.
Broad surface variation, flat brass and limited contact shading give a simplified illustrative finish.
entries.framing: All four originals contain the full object and raised tab; mobile title wraps and controls remain visible without obvious horizontal clipping.
entries.reason: Courtyard motif and hardware identity retained, no definite visible breakage or framing defect; stepped joints remain a static inspection limitation.

observed_defects.observation: Pale projecting rim ends and stepped/offset dark strips, especially at the right/rear corner, make the open rim look unfinished.
observed_defects.certainty: Visible presentation concern, not confirmed broken mesh, missing material or mechanical failure.

geometry_observations: Closed views preserve two faceted mountains, cracked pale salt basin, rippled body, clasp/disc, side ring and short feet. Salt polygon lines are intentional detail rather than damage.
Open desktop/mobile show hollow cavity and raised lid, but hinge seating appears visually separated; concealed attachment prevents a claim of disconnection.
Closed seam is prominent in both viewer and marketing; no unequivocal missing faces or major intersection demonstrated.
finish_limitations: Repetitive waves and subdued reflections make viewer copper read as clay/wood; marketing is softer dusty pink with more reflective fittings.
Terrain maintains two masses and white basin but viewer treatment is coarser/warmer than the gray reference peaks. Interior depth separation is weak.
entries.framing: Full object and controls fit desktop/mobile with no obvious clipping or overflow; small hardware limits inspection.
entries.reason: Open-rim presentation warrants user acceptance or closer alternate-angle review. Preserve the parent hold even without proven geometry failure; do not turn hinge uncertainty into a mechanical defect claim.
